status.label: Confirm Windows-hotkey remap overlap
status.detail: The report overlaps open Game Bar and system-hotkey remap reports, but its three-key remap sequence may be distinct.

judgment.rationale: The reporter says a Win/Alt/Ctrl remap cycle still triggers the Xbox Game Bar broadcasting panel through a Windows hotkey, even after disabling the apparent shortcut. Open issues #29969 and #26001 describe remapped Win/Alt keys still invoking Game Bar or other Windows hotkeys, so this report may be a variant of the same tracked behavior. Its three-remap cycle and Win+Alt+W trigger are not yet shown to be covered. The report is open and unassigned.
evidence: The report lists PowerToys 0.92.1 from the Microsoft Store and gives a three-key left Alt/Win/Ctrl remap.
The reporter says pressing the remapped Win key still opens the deprecated Game Bar broadcasting panel despite disabling the Windows+Alt+W shortcut.
Open issue #29969 reports remapped Win/Alt keys still triggering Game Bar, including Win+G; open issue #26001 reports remapping being overridden by built-in Windows hotkeys.
The issue has one similar-issues bot comment, is open, and has no assignee.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask whether the issue persists on current stable and whether the simpler Win/Alt swap from #29969 reproduces the same behavior; consolidate if it does, otherwise investigate the three-remap interaction.

fix_assessment.rationale: The report says a Windows Game Bar hotkey fires through a remapped Win key, which aligns with the open #29969 and #26001 reports. A remap-order or raw-key precedence defect is plausible, but the three-key cycle and current-version result are not yet isolated.

proposed_fixes.title: Prevent raw Windows hotkeys from bypassing active key remaps
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The Windows shell may observe the original Win-key state before Keyboard Manager's remapped state takes effect, allowing a Game Bar chord to fire despite the configured mapping. Similar behavior is already tracked in #29969 and #26001; this report may add a three-remap edge case.
plan: Confirm the issue on current stable and compare the reported three-remap cycle with the simpler Win/Alt swap from #29969.
If the simpler swap reproduces the same Game Bar behavior, consolidate the three-remap evidence into the existing open issue instead of creating competing implementation work.
If the failure is unique to the three-remap cycle, trace the ordering and modifier state of the three left-key mappings.
Add regression coverage ensuring the configured remap, not the raw Windows key, determines the triggered shell chord.
verification: Verify the remapped key does not trigger the unintended Game Bar broadcasting shortcut on current stable.
Verify the intended remapped key behavior still works and unrelated Windows shortcuts remain available.
Compare the three-remap sequence with the simpler Win/Alt swap to establish whether one existing issue covers both.

confidence.rationale: Two open reports describe the same class of raw Windows hotkey overlap, but the current issue's three-key cycle may introduce a distinct interaction.

issue_context.summary: A three-key left Alt/Win/Ctrl remap reportedly still allows the Xbox Game Bar broadcasting hotkey to fire through the remapped Win key.
known_information: The report lists PowerToys 0.92.1 from the Microsoft Store.
The reporter maps left Alt to Ctrl, left Win to Alt, and left Ctrl to Win.
The reporter says the deprecated Game Bar broadcasting panel opens despite disabling the Windows+Alt+W shortcut.
Open issues #29969 and #26001 describe related Game Bar or built-in Windows hotkey overlap with remapped keys.
inferences: The shell may receive the original Win state before the remapped state, but the reported three-key sequence has not been compared with the simpler configuration in the related issues.
issue_context.analysis: The likely issue class is already tracked in two open reports, so this should not create a competing fix until the unique three-remap aspect is established. The exact current-version result and comparison with a simple Win/Alt swap determine whether this is duplicate evidence or a distinct remap-order defect.
initial_investigation: Read the live issue body and its similar-issues comment, current labels, state, assignees, and discussion.
Read open issue #29969, which reports remapped Win/Alt keys triggering Game Bar, and #26001, which reports built-in Windows hotkeys overriding remaps.
The related issues are open and describe overlapping behavior, but no linked fix or exact three-remap comparison was found.

information_gaps.information: Whether the reported behavior persists on current stable PowerToys
information_gaps.why_needed: The issue is from version 0.92.1, and a later release may have changed system-hotkey handling.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Repeat the reported remap on current stable and state the exact PowerToys version and result.

information_gaps.information: Whether the same Game Bar behavior occurs with only the left Win/left Alt swap
information_gaps.why_needed: This determines whether #29969 covers the current issue or whether the additional Ctrl remap changes the outcome.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Compare the three-remap cycle with a simple left Win/left Alt swap using the same Game Bar shortcut.

comment.body:
Thanks for listing the three left-key remaps and the Game Bar shortcut that still fires. Open issues #29969 and #26001 describe similar Windows hotkey overlap, but they do not establish whether your three-remap sequence is covered. Could you confirm:
1. Whether the issue still occurs on current stable PowerToys and the exact version tested.
2. Whether the same Game Bar behavior occurs with only a left Win/left Alt swap, or only with the full three-remap cycle.

That comparison will show whether this is additional evidence for an existing report or a distinct interaction.

actions.label: Approve the Windows-hotkey remap fix direction
